ch30.f.d.scenario: A square loop crossing a field region, or a bar magnet passing through a coil (side view)
ch30.f.d.v: Speed $v$ of the loop or the magnet
ch30.f.d.B: Uniform field $B$ inside the region (out of the page)
ch30.f.goal.law: Faraday's law: the induced emf is $\mathcal{E} = -d\Phi_B/dt$; the rate of change of the flux, not the flux itself, drives it
ch30.f.goal.lenz: Lenz's law: the field $B_\text{ind}$ of the induced current opposes the change in flux
ch30.f.obs.enter: Loop entering the region: $\Phi_B$ grows, so $\mathcal{E} < 0$, a clockwise current, and $B_\text{ind}$ into the page inside the loop (⊗)
ch30.f.obs.full: Loop entirely inside: $\Phi_B$ is constant, $\mathcal{E} = 0$, no current
ch30.f.obs.leave: Loop leaving: $\Phi_B$ falls, so $\mathcal{E} > 0$, a counter-clockwise current, $B_\text{ind}$ out of the page (⊙)
ch30.f.obs.slope: The tangent to $\Phi_B(t)$ has slope $d\Phi_B/dt$; the dot on the lower plot is minus that slope (pause and move along the plot to compare)
ch30.f.obs.magnet: Magnet through the coil: the emf has opposite signs while approaching and receding, and is 0 with the magnet at the centre
ch30.f.obs.v: Double the speed: the same flux change takes half the time, so $\mathcal{E}$ doubles
ch30.f.as.region: Square loop of side $a = 0.4$ m, region 1 m wide; the field drops to 0 sharply at the region edge
ch30.f.as.magnet: The magnet is a point dipole with moment $m = 100\ \mathrm{A\,m^2}$; coil radius 0.2 m, one turn
ch30.f.as.sign: Flux reference direction: out of the page (region), to the right, $+x$ (magnet). $\mathcal{E} > 0$ drives current that circles that direction by the right-hand rule
ch30.f.as.self: The flux of the induced current's own field (self-inductance) is neglected
ch30.m.d.eq: Equation to look at: Gauss (electric), Gauss (magnetic), Faraday, Ampère-Maxwell
ch30.m.d.dBdt: Rate of increase of the uniform field inside the disc (out of the page)
ch30.m.d.surf: Surface bounded by the same loop: a flat disc, or a bag reaching between the capacitor plates
ch30.m.goal.four: The four Maxwell equations: the sources of $E$ and $B$ (charge; no monopoles) and how each field makes the other (changing $B$ → $E$; currents and changing $E$ → $B$)
ch30.m.goal.pairs: Flux through a closed surface (the two Gauss laws) and circulation around a closed path (Faraday, Ampère-Maxwell)
ch30.m.obs.gaussE: Gauss (electric): the electric flux through a closed surface is the enclosed charge over $\varepsilon_0$; outside charges add nothing
ch30.m.obs.gaussB: Gauss (magnetic): field lines are closed loops with no start or end, so any closed surface has as much flux out as in; no monopoles
ch30.m.obs.faraday: Faraday: a changing magnetic field makes an electric field that circles around (not conservative); its circulation is $-d\Phi_B/dt$
ch30.m.obs.ampere: Ampère-Maxwell: on the same loop, the flat surface is crossed by the conduction current $i$, the bag by the displacement current $\varepsilon_0\,d\Phi_E/dt$ between the plates; both give $\mu_0 i$
ch30.m.obs.drag: Drag the centre point of a circle to move it and its edge point to resize it; drag charges to move them. In Ampère-Maxwell drag the point above the loop to move the loop
ch30.m.as.2d: Gauss (electric): cross-section of line charges perpendicular to the page (flux per unit length)
ch30.m.as.magnet: Magnet: a uniformly magnetised bar represented by its bound surface currents (⊙ on top, ⊗ below, 30 each), 2D section
ch30.m.as.faraday: Faraday: the field changes uniformly inside a disc of radius 0.35 m only; $E$ arrow lengths are a log scale
ch30.m.as.cap: Ampère-Maxwell: disc capacitor (plate radius 0.3 m) charged by a 2 A current, loop radius 0.4 m, fringing neglected
